To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
polymorphisms of the MTHFR, MTRR, TYMS and MTR genes were significantly associated with the risk of APL, AML, ALL, and MDS.

the MTRR and TYMS polymorphisms are associated with increased risk of AML, the MTHFR polymorphism is associated with increased risk in ALL, and the MTR and TYMS polymophisms are associated with risk of MDS in the Korean population.
the risk for ALC was associated with the MTHR 677 polymorphism and that the risk for MDS was associated the MTRR66 polymorphism and the risk for ALL was associated with the hap C polymorphism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the association of genetic polymorphisms of the folate-metabolic enzymes with the risk of hematological malignancies in the Korean population.
the association of folate polymorphisims with the risk for APL, CML, ALL and MDS.

the association between folate polymorphims and the risk for hematological malignancies in Korea and provides a basis for further research on the role of genetic factors in the etiology of hematologic malignancies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the MTHFR polymorphism was associated with an elevated risk for ALL, the MTRR polymorphism was associated an increased risk for both AML and MDS and TYMS polymorphism was associated a reduced risk for AML.
the MTHFR, MTRR, TYMS, MTR, MTHFD1, and RFC1 polymorphisms are not associated with the risk for APL, ALL, CML, and MDS in Korea.

polymorphisms of the folate-metabolic pathway may modify the risk of hematological malignancies, and further study is required to clarify the relationship between folate polymorphism and hematologic malignancies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
polymorphisms in MTHFR, MTRR, and TYMS are associated with the risk for ALL.
the MTHFR polymorphisms may modify the risk of ALL and the MTR and TYMS polymorphisms may influence the risk of APL and AML, respectively.
the polymorphisms in folate-metabolic enzymes may be associated with the risk of hematological malignancies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
folate metabolism is important for the development of several hematologic malignanices.
folate polymorphims play an important role in the etiology of hematological malignancies in Korea.
folate-metabolic polymorphisms are associated with the risk of several hematologic malignancy.
